correctness.rationale: The unique first seat is the maximum support for both rules. Direct derivation of the second-step PAV marginal and Phragmén total load produces inequalities (1). Integer cases for equal, greater, and smaller remaining-candidate support exclude all n<9 and all other n=9 profiles. The displayed nine-voter ballot profile satisfies strict inequalities, and C-only voter additions preserve them for every larger electorate. The self-contained exact-rational checker verifies all 11,439 anonymous profiles at n<=9 independently by each algorithm; 6 strict disagreements, precisely one orbit.

originality.rationale: The exact n=9 cutoff, its six-profile complete classification, and the all-size witness extension are more specific than the established existence of large separating examples and are not deduced by those examples alone. Closest paper Janson 2016, Section 13, already documents that the rules disagree and even supplies a two-seat example with much larger vote counts. The exact minimal strict profile classification was not identified in the accessible primary literature searches, with residual publication-priority risk explicitly retained.
residual_risks: An unlocated or inaccessible exact minimization/census theorem could cover the nine-voter cutoff; neither keyword searches nor a semantic database search proves universal novelty.
The core historical paper already includes similar qualitative two-seat disagreements, so the priority claim is confined to the strict sharp minimum and complete first orbit.
Other definitions of Phragmén or different tie-breaking conventions can give different answers; the result uses the precise standard greedy voter-load rule.

value.rationale: The candidate count three and two-seat committee are the first possible nontrivial domain in which these two proportional approval algorithms can disagree: k=1 is identical approval voting and m=k=2 elects all candidates. The sharp nine-voter electorate threshold and complete one-orbit classification precisely identify the first genuine distinction and provide a tiny canonical test instance. The result clarifies the mathematical cost-sharing distinction underlying established large examples rather than choosing an arbitrary finite sample.
